description: Priesthoods became entrenched within ancient social and political hierarchies because religious authority was closely tied to government, landholding, law, and communal identity. Temples often controlled substantial wealth and property, while priests supervised sacrifices, festivals, divination, calendars, and rituals believed necessary for maintaining divine favor and social order. Rulers strengthened their legitimacy by supporting established cults, and elite families frequently monopolized important priestly offices, allowing religious positions to become hereditary or politically prestigious. Over time, this combination of sacred authority, economic influence, and close association with ruling institutions gave many priesthoods a durable place near the top of ancient society.
